# hired.video — Shipped & Resolved Archive

> Moved out of [README.md](README.md) on 2026-06-20 to keep the README focused on **open + partial** work. This file holds the shipped-capability summary plus every ✅ Done / Removed / Won't-fix / Superseded gap-register row. Gap IDs (`#NNNN`) remain globally unique, so historical references still resolve here. The live **Consolidated Gap Register** (open + partial only) stays in the README.

## Done — Shipped Capability Summary

This consolidates the **579 ✅ Done entries** from the Consolidated Gap Register into thematic clusters. Each cluster is a domain of work that has been shipped. Individual Done entries have been removed from the register below to keep it focused on **open + partial** work. ID ranges in parentheses preserve the original entry numbers so historical follow-up references (`#NNNN`) still resolve.

> If you're looking for an item that used to be in the register: the gap ID still exists in the codebase / commit history; only the register row has been archived here.

Microsoft codes (AADSTS70000/AADSTS50173/AADSTS50076/interaction_required/consent_required/login_required) now route to the reauth banner instead of the 502 toast. **Original:** **`MAILBOX_REAUTH_REQUIRED` is detected via a regex match on Google's `invalid_grant` substring — Microsoft Graph returns at least three more codes (`AADSTS70000`, `interaction_required`, `consent_required`) that today's classifier mis-routes to the generic `REFRESH_FAILED` 502 toast** (opened 2026-05-21 — surfaced fixing the Gmail-specific case at [email-integration.ts /accounts/:id/access-token](hired.video/api/src/routes/email-integration.ts)) | [refreshAccessToken in oauth.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/email-integration/oauth.ts) throws an `Error` whose message is the raw provider response body. Today's route at [email-integration.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/email-integration.ts) checks `/invalid_grant/i.test(message)` to flip to `MAILBOX_REAUTH_REQUIRED` — Google + Outlook both use that string most of the time, but Microsoft Graph also emits `AADSTS70000` (refresh token rejected — revoked/expired), `AADSTS50173` (recent password change, fresh sign-in required), `interaction_required`, and `consent_required`. Centralises the provider-specific classifier in one place instead of leaking strings through the throw. Unblocks: Outlook users get the same Reconnect banner instead of a red 502 + Support Ticket prompt on every Microsoft re-auth needed. |

| 1522 | ✅ Done | Now | P1 | `bug` | **Seeded `md5(slug)::uuid` IDs fail Zod 4 `.uuid()` validation — every route that strict-validated a DB-row UUID rejected seed-derived rows** (opened + fully fixed 2026-05-26 after a support ticket: PATCH `/api/courses/enrollments/:id/progress` returned 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` "Invalid UUID" with body `{ lessonId: "c87f7656-673a-7756-d100-281032a50731", … }` — that lesson is from [0131_seed_platform_learning_library.sql](hired.video/api/drizzle/0131_seed_platform_learning_library.sql) which uses `md5('seed-lesson:…')::uuid` for deterministic IDs). Root cause: Zod 4's `.uuid()` regex requires the variant nibble to be `[89abAB]` (RFC 4122), but MD5 hashes land on any nibble — the user's lesson ID has variant `d`. Same seed pattern is in [0113_so_you_want_to_become_articles.sql](hired.video/api/drizzle/0113_so_you_want_to_become_articles.sql) for seeded articles. **Fix**: introduced `UuidLikeSchema` + `UUID_LIKE_REGEX` in [shared/validation.ts](hired.video/shared/validation.ts) (permissive 8-4-4-4-12 hex, no version/variant constraint) and **swept the entire codebase** — 270 call sites across 57 files in `api/src/` + `shared/` migrated from `z.string().uuid()` → `UuidLikeSchema` (the two custom-message callers in [superadmin/sessions.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/superadmin/sessions.ts) + [superadmin/users.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/superadmin/users.ts) preserve their messages via `z.string().regex(UUID_LIKE_REGEX, "…")`). Strict `UuidSchema` is kept in shared/validation.ts for IDs generated fresh in app code; doc comment in the file pins the split. **Latent Zod-4 bug also fixed in the same pass**: two `z.record(z.unknown())` calls in [courses.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/courses.ts) (ScormCommitSchema.cmi, XapiStatementSchema.context) were silently broken under Zod 4 (which requires `z.record(key, value)`); both now `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`. **Pre-existing fixture bug fixed in the same pass**: [resume-contract.test.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/__tests__/resume-contract.test.ts) was missing `archivedAt: null` on its base fixture; added. **Tests added** (3 new test files + 1 shared fixture module, 72 cases total — closes the test-coverage gap that masked this bug): (a) [shared/__tests__/validation.test.ts](hired.video/shared/__tests__/validation.test.ts) — 25 cases pinning `UuidSchema` strict + `UuidLikeSchema` permissive + raw regex against the prod-incident UUID, runtime v4s, RFC v1/v7, nil/max, uppercase, shape-length drift, non-hex, whitespace, null/undefined/numbers; (b) [api/src/routes/__tests__/courses-schemas.test.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/__tests__/courses-schemas.test.ts) — 38 cases against `ProgressUpdateSchema`, `ScormCommitSchema`, `XapiStatementSchema`, `PrerequisiteSchema`, `CreateLessonSchema` (happy + boundary + exception, with explicit md5-seed-derived UUID fixtures); (c) [api/src/routes/__tests__/learning-paths-schemas.test.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/__tests__/learning-paths-schemas.test.ts) — 9 cases against `AttachCourseSchema`; (d) [shared/__tests__/uuid-fixtures.ts](hired.video/shared/__tests__/uuid-fixtures.ts) — DRY fixture module (`V4_UUID`, `SEED_DERIVED_UUID`, `V1_UUID`, `V7_UUID_RFC`, `NIL_UUID`, `MAX_UUID`, `SYNTHETIC_V4_UUID`, `SHAPE_FAILURES`) consumed by all four test files including the pre-existing scorecards `schemas.test.ts`. The relevant route schemas were promoted from `const` to `export const` so the tests can import them. **Dead-code cleanup in the same pass** (per the "no orphan exports" rule): validation.ts went from 432 → 78 lines after removing `UserLocationSchema`, `UserContactSchema`, `UserExperienceSchema`, `UserEducationSchema`, `UserSkillSchema`, `UserProjectSchema`, `UserDataSchema`, `CompanyDataSchema`, `JobDataSchema`, `ResumeBasicsSchema`, `ResumeWorkSchema`, `ResumeEducationSchema`, `ResumeSkillsSchema`, `ResumeDataSchema`, `UrlSchema`, `DateSchema`, `OptionalNonEmptyStringSchema` + their 10 `*Validated` type aliases — every one had zero callers outside validation.ts itself. The frontend has its own local `CompanyDataSchema` so nothing was orphaned. Retained: `UuidSchema`, `UuidLikeSchema`, `UUID_LIKE_REGEX`, `OptionalUrlSchema` (used by jobs.ts + studio.ts), `NonEmptyStringSchema` + `EmailSchema` (both used by `shared/account.ts` invite metadata). **Two pre-existing frontend tsc errors fixed in the same pass** (build was failing on 2026-05-26 prior to this commit): (a) [wcag-audit.ts:287](hired.video/frontend/lib/studio/accessibility/wcag-audit.ts#L287) — `WidgetParams` discriminated-union cast widened via `unknown` because the variant `*WidgetParams` types lack index signatures; (b) [paint.ts:23](hired.video/frontend/lib/studio/avatar/paint.ts#L23) — `paintPresenter` / `paintHair` / `paintMouth` accept `CanvasRenderingContext2D | OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D` so the timeline frame renderer in [canvas-v2.ts:1724](hired.video/frontend/lib/timeline/effects/canvas-v2.ts#L1724) can call them off either context. **Final verification**: full api suite 1690 pass / 0 fail; frontend `tsc` clean. Open follow-ups tracked as #1527 (ESLint guard) + #1528 (schema-test backfill). |

| 1566 | ✅ Done | Now | P1 | `bug` | **Course completion never fired for text_md-only courses (the 5 platform-seed courses)** (resolved 2026-05-26 — user-reported: "4 of 4 lessons complete" but course stayed `in progress`, no cert, no badge, no celebration). Backfill cert auto-issue runs once per enrollment on first load when `passed && !certificate && issuesCertificate`. Pinned by 9 unit tests in [course-completion.test.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/learning/__tests__/course-completion.test.ts) covering the unscored-course carve-out + scored-mixed + threshold + idempotency. |

| 1578 | ✅ Done | Now | P1 | `bug` | **`POST /api/ai/chat` 500 on `ai_chat_messages` insert — user-visible chat now resilient (best-effort persistence + early user-write), diagnostic surface live, root cause still pending next repro** (opened 2026-05-26 from two live INTERNAL_ERROR support tickets ~5 min apart, sessions `91a5a4dc-…` + `73993c7c-…`, same Career-Coach interview-practice prompt, identical `tokens_used: 5069`; reporter confirmed it 500s on **every** chat click before the fix below). What the user saw was the literal SQL of the failed insert prefixed with `Failed query: …` — i.e. Drizzle's wrapper message — with **zero PG error code, constraint, or detail**, because [globalErrorHandler](hired.video/api/src/middleware/errorHandler.ts) only forwarded `err.message` and dropped `err.cause`. Without the cause, we cannot tell whether the failure is (a) FK violation on `session_id` (most likely — session row never committed, or replica-lag race between the SELECT at [ai.ts:145-155](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts#L145-L155) and the INSERT at [ai.ts:262](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts#L262)), (b) a transient Neon HTTP write failure, or (c) a constraint we didn't anticipate. Schema itself is permissive — `content text` unbounded, `role varchar(20)` fits `"user"`, `tokens_used int4 nullable` fits 5069 — so a schema-level rejection is ruled out from the surfaced data. **Shipped this pass:** (1) [errorHandler.ts](hired.video/api/src/middleware/errorHandler.ts) now extracts PG diagnostic fields (`code`, `detail`, `hint`, `schema`, `table`, `column`, `dataType`, `constraint`, `routine`) from `err` + walks up to four levels of `err.cause`, attaches them as `_pg` on the response envelope, and includes them in the structured server log. (2) [errorSourceFilter.ts](hired.video/api/src/middleware/errorSourceFilter.ts) generalised from a `_source`-only stripper to a `SUPERADMIN_ONLY_ERROR_FIELDS` allowlist, so the new `_pg` field is SuperAdmin-only by the same rule. (3) Adjacent security gap closed in the same pass: the session-validation path at [ai.ts:145-155](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts#L145-L155) now filters by `(id, userId)` instead of `id` alone — pre-fix, any authenticated user could POST a turn into another user's session by guessing/observing the UUID, leaking content + corrupting their history. (4) **User-visible chat fix:** the two `ai_chat_messages` inserts now go through a single `persistChatMessage(role, content, tokensUsed)` helper at [ai.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts) (DRY — one try/catch site, one log line shape). User message persists BEFORE the LLM dispatch (when subrequest budget is still flush — see #1570 for the dispatch chain's per-invocation cost); assistant message persists AFTER. Both are wrapped in try/catch — failure logs `[ai/chat] persist message failed` with `{sessionId, role, tokensUsed, err}` and **does not 500 the route**. Chat appears to work even when persistence is broken; the history just loses that turn (recoverable: the LLM-generated answer is in the response body, the user's prompt is still in the request body the client just sent). Dead `let model = "mock"` (assigned but never read) dropped while restructuring. **Still open:** root cause — wait for the next `console.error("[ai/chat] persist message failed", …)` log with the new `_pg` surface live to confirm whether the failure class is FK / replica-lag / transient / subrequest-cap-exhaustion, then either (i) wrap session-resolve + message-insert in a Neon HTTP transaction so they share a connection + snapshot (FK race), (ii) retry once on Neon transient classes, or (iii) trim USE_CASE_PROFILES["chat"] / strip non-essential middleware off this route to free subrequests (#1570 root cause). **Out of scope this pass (recorded):** `tokens_used: 5069` for a ~2 KB visible prompt looks high but is plausibly correct — it's `result.usage.promptTokens` from the LLM at [ai.ts:227](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts#L227), which includes the system prompt + last 20 history messages loaded at [ai.ts:175-183](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts#L175-L183); not worth changing without a confirmed mis-count from the gateway. **Adjacent:** the diagnostic improvement here helps every DB-layer 500 across the API, not just AI chat. |

| 1590 | ✅ Done | — | — | `bug` | **apiClient retried server-side failures with exponential backoff, amplifying a CPU-exhausted worker's load by 4×** (closed 2026-05-26 alongside the save-draft 503 sweep). | 1912 | ✅ Done | Now | P1 | `bug` | **Studio render OOM-crashes the renderer (no WebCodecs encoder backpressure) — surfaced as "Render worker crashed" on Publish-to-YouTube** (opened+fixed 2026-06-05) | The WebCodecs compose loop in [webcodecs-render.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/timeline/webcodecs-render.ts) `runEncodeWorker()` posted every composited frame to the encode worker as fast as it could composite, and the worker ([render-encode.worker.ts](hired.video/frontend/workers/render-encode.worker.ts)) called `videoEncoder.encode()` per message with **no `encodeQueueSize` check**. When compositing outruns a software AVC encoder (fast/cached seeks on a fully-buffered local blob — e.g. a screen-share capture — or a source-less canvas/animation timeline), the encoder's queue of multi-MB `VideoFrame`s grows without bound until the renderer process OOM-crashes. Signature the user hit: the tab's `chrome-error://chromewebdata/` page + AdSense scripts failing from that dead frame + "AudioContext encountered an error from the audio device" + `worker.onerror` → "render worker crashed". **Fixed 2026-06-05:** credit-based backpressure — the worker reports `encodeQueueSize` on every admit (handleFrame) and every drain (the encoder `output` callback); the compositor pauses producing at HIGH_WATER=12 and resumes at LOW_WATER=6, bounding peak in-flight frames regardless of timeline length or encoder speed. `cleanup()` wakes a parked compositor so a worker error can't hang it. Typecheck clean. **NOT yet runtime-verified** against the user's actual project. |
| 1913 | ✅ Done | Soon | P3 | `bug` | **MediaRecorder screen-capture WebM reports `duration === Infinity`; per-frame `seekTo` is a latent hang risk on render** (opened 2026-06-05 alongside #1912, fixed 2026-06-06) | Screen recordings are captured via MediaRecorder ([use-screen-recording.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/studio/editor-v2/use-screen-recording.ts), VP9/Opus WebM on Chromium). Such blobs carry no WebM Duration element, so when the render path loads the (R2-served) blob into a `<video>`, `video.duration` is `Infinity`. Clip duration is safe (the editor stamps the recorder's finite wall-clock `durationSeconds` via `addMediaWidget`, never `video.duration`), so `totalFrames` is bounded — but [frame-renderer.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/timeline/frame-renderer.ts) `seekTo()` computed `Math.min(video.duration || time, time)` (= `time` when duration is `Infinity`, so a seek could land past the real EOF) and relied on the `seeked` event firing, which may never happen — hanging the compose loop. **Fixed 2026-06-06** with both belts: (a) `repairInfiniteDuration()` runs once per source at preload in `createMediaElement` — seeks to a `1e7` sentinel, awaits `durationchange`/`seeked` until `video.duration` is finite, resets to 0 (the canonical MediaRecorder-WebM workaround), bounded by a 5 s timeout so a degenerate source can't stall preload; the finite-duration guard makes it a no-op for normal videos. (b) `seekTo()` now bounds its `seeked` await with a 3 s timeout that resolves-and-draws the current decoded frame, so no single seek can ever hang the render. Typecheck clean; existing frame-renderer tests pass. (No unit test added — `seekTo`/duration-repair are event-driven on a real `<video>` element; jsdom's video stub would test the mock, not the behavior.) Unblocks: robust render of screen-capture clips without a hang. |
| 1914 | ✅ Done | Now | P1 | `bug` | **CI `vite build` OOM-crashes (heap limit) while minifying the 6.4k-module bundle** (opened+fixed 2026-06-05) | The "Build SPA" step (`cd frontend && npm run build`) died with `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed` at ~2090 MB during the "rendering chunks" phase — Node's ~2 GB default old-space ceiling, which the large bundle + terser minify exceed (the `JsonParse` frame in the trace was just the straw, not the cause). **Fixed 2026-06-05:** (a) [ci.yml](hired.video/.github/workflows/ci.yml) Build SPA step sets `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144` (ubuntu-latest has 16 GB); (b) [vite.config.ts](hired.video/frontend/vite.config.ts) now runs `rollup-plugin-visualizer` only under `ANALYZE=true` — gzip+brotli-sizing every chunk + retaining per-module metadata on every build was needless CI memory/CPU (its `stats.html` is precache-excluded and unused by deploys), so it also shaves the 8m+ build time. The genuine fix — reducing the shipped bundle (lazy-load remaining heavy deps `three`/`pdfjs-dist`/`leaflet`, eager `BLOG_POSTS`) — remains tracked under #1341. Unblocks: green CI build + deploy. |

| 1953 | ✅ Done | Now | P3 | `bug` | **Orphaned live `AudioContext`s spam "The AudioContext encountered an error from the audio device or the WebAudio renderer" on unrelated pages** (found 2026-06-07 via user console report on `/search?category=media`) | Several surfaces created ad-hoc `new AudioContext()` device-backed contexts; the worst offender, [tts-engines.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/services/tts-engines.ts) `playPcm()`, stashed a module-scope `activeWebAudioCtx` that `clearWebAudio()` never closed — so after any WebGPU TTS narration in the studio the context outlived the SPA navigation and, when the OS audio device hiccuped (sleep / device switch / exclusive grab), re-emitted Chromium's verbatim device error on whatever page the user was now on (here a no-audio media-search page). Routed all 5 interactive/long-lived creators through it ([use-music-scheduler.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/audio/use-music-scheduler.ts), [ambient-player.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/audio/ambient-player.ts) `play()` path, [tts-engines.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/services/tts-engines.ts), [PianoComposer.tsx](hired.video/frontend/components/studio/music/PianoComposer.tsx), [WebcamRecorder.tsx](hired.video/frontend/components/studio/WebcamRecorder.tsx)) — each now `release()`s on stop/unmount so no idle device handle lingers. Deliberately left as-is: the self-contained export pipeline ([video-exporter.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/renderer/video-exporter.ts), owns its own MediaStreamDestination + user-facing `RenderAudioContextError` + closes its ctx — the reference impl this pattern generalizes) and the transient decode-then-close context in [beat-detection.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/sizzle/beat-detection.ts); `OfflineAudioContext` render paths never touch the device. tsc + lint clean (0 errors). **NOT yet runtime-verified** — the exact device error couldn't be reproduced here; re-check by exercising studio TTS/music then navigating to `/search?category=media`. Related but distinct: #718 (render-path `RenderAudioContextError` telemetry enrichment, still open). |

| 2195 | ✅ Done | Now | P2 | `bug` | **Helcim webhook HMAC used a non-constant-time string compare (timing-oracle risk)** (found + closed 2026-06-16, TK2) | [helcim.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/billing/payment/helcim.ts) `verifyWebhook` compared the computed HMAC with `signature !== expected` — a `!==` short-circuits on the first wrong byte, so response timing could be used as a signature oracle (Stripe's path is constant-time internally). **Fix:** switched to `crypto.timingSafeEqual` with a length guard (the 64-char hex digest makes a length mismatch an outright rejection). 7 new tests ([helcim-webhook.test.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/billing/payment/__tests__/helcim-webhook.test.ts)) cover valid/forged/tampered/wrong-length/missing-header/missing-token + event-type normalisation. |

| 2244 | ✅ Done | Now | P2 | `bug` | **Roaming `# pass N / # fail 1` CI flake = a real ~1/256 base64url tamper edge case in `certificate-signing.test.ts` (NOT node:test cross-attribution — that was the #2241 mis-diagnosis)** (root-caused + fixed 2026-06-22; supersedes the open flake entry formerly mis-numbered #2241, which collided with the shipped studio-deep-link #2241 in this file) | The `CertificateService.verify — Ed25519 (3-part)` › "rejects a tampered Ed25519 signature" subtest corrupted the signature with `sig.slice(0,-2) + (sig.endsWith("A") ? "BB" : "AA")`. A 64-byte Ed25519 sig is 86 base64url chars whose FINAL char carries only 2 significant bits (4 "don't-care" padding bits), so that tamper only mutates the last byte — and when the random sig's last byte was exactly `4`, the `"BB"` replacement decoded back to the SAME bytes → unchanged sig → the (correct) verifier accepted it → `valid:true` ≠ expected `false`. ~1/256 per run → the rare roaming red (reproduced locally on run 5/5, exact same `not ok 559` as CI job 82844995155). The HMAC tamper test shared the identical fragile pattern (latent). **Fix:** extracted a shared `tamperSig = (sig)=>(sig[0]==="A"?"B":"A")+sig.slice(1)` in [certificate-signing.test.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/learning/__tests__/certificate-signing.test.ts) — flips byte 0 (always fully significant), deterministic real tamper for BOTH the Ed25519 and HMAC paths. The service ([certificate-service.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/learning/certificate-service.ts)) was correct and unchanged. Verified 60×9 = 540 green (old code would flake ~21% across 60 runs). Lesson: not every `# fail 1` is a timer flake — a 1/256 data-dependent assertion (random key/sig/uuid) reds just as rarely; loop the SUSPECT file 30-60× before blaming the runner. |

Marked deferred rather than open so it stops appearing in audit re-runs. | (opened 2026-05-26 from gap-#1594 audit). Documented offenders (each acceptable until you need to filter by them): [usage.ts](hired.video/api/src/db/schema/usage.ts) `usageStatements.lines` (array of line-items — fine for display, blocks "find all statements with line X" queries); [assessments.ts:55](hired.video/api/src/db/schema/assessments.ts#L55) `assessmentAttempts.gradingResults` (per-question feedback); [calibration.ts:42-45](hired.video/api/src/db/schema/calibration.ts#L42-L45) `calibrationSessions.candidateApplicationIds` (text-array of FKs — N+1 to load); [gamification.ts:282](hired.video/api/src/db/schema/gamification.ts#L282) `pointRedemptions.grantPayload` (status filter has to deserialize). **Fix**: this is the "don't normalize until you need to" entry — track which JSON blobs grow queryable demand and extract to junction tables on demand. **Unblocks**: nothing right now; flagged so future "I need to query by X inside this JSON" doesn't surprise us. |
| 1610-original | ⚠️ Original | — | — | `smell` | **Polymorphic ownership: studio uses `(ownerType, ownerId)` pair, interview-question-sets uses XOR nullables** (opened 2026-05-26 from gap-#1594 audit — [studiofeatures.ts:498](hired.video/api/src/db/schema/studiofeatures.ts#L498)). `interviewQuestionSets.ownerUserId` + `ownerCompanyId` both nullable with "XOR" intent — same anti-pattern that [project_studio_workspaces](memory/project_studio_workspaces.md) already standardized away for studio_projects via `canActFor()`. Should align to the canonical `(owner_type, owner_id)` pair the studio aggregate uses. Same pattern in [jobboards.ts:51-74](hired.video/api/src/db/schema/jobboards.ts#L51-L74) `boardBids` (one of `boardId` / `jobId` must be NOT NULL, but no CHECK enforces it). **Fix**: introduce `(owner_type, owner_id)` columns + CHECK constraint enforcing both NOT NULL; backfill from the old XOR pair; drop the old pair. **Unblocks**: makes interview-question-set ownership routable through the same `canActFor()` SSoT as studio assets, instead of two separate code paths. |
| 1650 | ❎ Deferred-by-design | — | — | `perf` | **Recruiter money `numeric` → `integer cents` — deferred** (resolved 2026-05-26). Conversion touches: recruiter.ts schema (~8 columns), every recruiter route that reads/writes the values (~12 callsites), DTOs that surface to the frontend (~6), commission engine math, analytics rollups. Storage savings of ~5-8 bytes/row at recruiter scale (~100K rows) is dwarfed by the callsite-rewrite cost AND the risk of breaking commission-engine precision (a 1-cent rounding error in a recruiter's payout is a support ticket). Revisit when (a) recruiter surface is in active production use AND (b) we're seeing real row-count growth on `placements`. For now `numeric` is the safer shape. | (opened 2026-05-26 from pass-9 compactness audit). [recruiter.ts](hired.video/api/src/db/schema/recruiter.ts) `proposedSalary`, `salary`, `annualSalary`, `fee`, `commissionAmount`, `commissionPercentage`, `billRateHourly`, `payRateHourly` use `numeric` (variable width, slow). [jobs.ts](hired.video/api/src/db/schema/jobs.ts) `salaryMin/salaryMax` same. Conversion to integer cents saves ~5-8 bytes/row at high-volume placement tables. Touches every recruiter route that reads these; defer until recruiter surface is in active use. **Unblocks**: tighter rows + index pages, faster comparisons, no float-to-decimal coercion in the analytics rollups. |
| 1651 | ❎ Deferred-by-design | — | — | `perf` | **Counter recompute incremental triggers — deferred** (resolved 2026-05-26). The daily UPDATE-with-IS-DISTINCT-FROM in [counter-recompute.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/maintenance/counter-recompute.ts) is O(N) once per day and only touches drifted rows; per-insert/delete triggers are O(1) per write but pay overhead on EVERY write — and write volume on the source tables (artifact_views, candidate_submissions, etc.) is far higher than read volume on the counters. Daily reconcile is the cheaper shape at current and projected scale. Switch when a single counter cache demonstrably crosses a measurable cost threshold (e.g. > 100M source rows AND > 1k counter-display reads/sec). Not happening at 1M users. | (opened 2026-05-26 from pass-9 scale audit). [services/maintenance/counter-recompute.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/maintenance/counter-recompute.ts) runs daily `UPDATE … SET col = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source …)`. At 100M+ rows in the source table, the COUNT(*) is non-trivial. Per-insert/delete triggers are faster (O(1) per write vs O(N) once per day) but require migration of every counter. Switch when a single counter cache crosses a measurable cost threshold — for now the daily recompute is cheaper than the trigger overhead given low write rates. **Unblocks**: linear-write counters that stay accurate without a daily reconcile. |

The polymorphic convention is `subject_type/subject_id` everywhere else, but `studio_project_subjects.subject_kind` predates the rule and is woven through routes/studio.ts (~7 callsites) + routes/course-authoring.ts + a public query-param contract (`?subjectKind=resume`). - **#1877 — `lessonId` deep-link scroll-to is unimplemented (dead comment)** — `CourseLearner.tsx`'s "Edit" button deep-links to `/services/creator/courses?courseId=…&lessonId=…` and `CoursesManagerPanel.tsx:167` claims "lessonId is consumed by CourseContentEditor (scroll-to)", but `CourseContentEditor` never reads `lessonId` — the param is silently ignored, so the author always lands at the top of the module tree instead of on the targeted lesson. (Surfaced while fixing the `getMine` envelope-shape crash on this same route, #1521.) Fixing it: forward `lessonId` from the panel into `CourseContentEditor`, give each lesson row a stable `id="lesson-row-<id>"`, and scroll/highlight it after load — makes the /learn → Edit handoff land on the right lesson.

- **#1878 — Studio CAD / 3D-CAD kinds have no left rail (no unit navigator, no tool palette)** — `StudioEditorV2.tsx`'s left `<CollapsiblePanel side="left">` only mounts for `image` (DrawingToolPalette), `game` (LevelsRail+SpritePalette), `animation` (FramesRail+DrawingToolPalette, added this pass), and `usesTimelineChrome` kinds (ScenesRail). `cad` / `cad_3d` fall through to NO left panel at all, and `<CadStage>` is mounted with a hardcoded `tool="select"` / `drawColor` / `drawStrokeWidthMm` — so the user can't switch tools, pick a layer, or change stroke from the editor chrome. (Surfaced while making the rail/playback pattern consistent across kinds — the animation report.) Fixing it: give cad/cad_3d the same left-panel shell with a CAD tool palette (and a layer/sheet list once CAD gains multiple sheets), lifting the tool/draw state into the host like image/animation. Unblocks consistent left-rail authoring for the CAD kinds.

- **#1879 — `interactive_comic` surface is never mounted; the kind silently falls back to the timeline canvas** — `mediaKindUsesCanvasStateAuthoring("interactive_comic")` returns `true`, so an interactive-comic project renders `ScenesRail` + the default `timeline` `CanvasStage`. But `<CanvasRouter>`'s `surfaces` prop in `StudioEditorV2.tsx` passes no `interactive_comic` slot, and there's no `interactiveComicState` hydration in the host — so `<InteractiveComicStage>` (the branching page-graph editor in `components/studio/comic/`) is dead code from the editor's perspective. The branching/reader model can't be authored. Fixing it: add an `interactiveComicState` history hook + hydration (mirror the animation/cad pattern), pass an `interactive_comic` surface to the router, and decide whether pages reuse ScenesRail or get their own graph rail. Unblocks actual interactive-comic authoring (#929).

- **#1880 — Animation `activeFrameId` lives in the history-tracked state, so selection + playback pollute undo** — `AnimationState.activeFrameId` is part of the persisted/`useCanvasHistory`-tracked shape, unlike video's `activeSceneId` (separate `useState`, untracked). Every frame click and every rAF playback advance calls the history-wrapped `setAnimationState`, which schedules a debounced commit — so undo/redo steps through frame selections and through playback, instead of through real edits. (Pre-existing; surfaced while lifting playback to the header this pass.) Fixing it: split the active-frame selection out of the tracked `AnimationState` into host `useState` (like `activeSceneId`), leaving only structural edits in history. Unblocks clean undo during animation editing/playback.

- **#1881 — Animation lacks DrawingStage's layer / marquee / inpaint capabilities** — animation now shares `DrawingToolPalette` (brush/eraser/fill/eyedropper + size/opacity/colour) with the image kind, but `AnimationFrame` has a single flat `pixelsDataUrl` — no per-frame layer stack, no marquee select, no AI inpaint, none of `<DrawingStage>`'s richer raster tooling. (`animation-state.ts` notes multi-layer-per-frame as a roadmap follow-on.) Fixing it: add an optional per-frame layer array to `AnimationState` (reusing `ImageLayer`), composite onion-skin + export from the flattened stack, and reuse DrawingStage's marquee/inpaint handlers. Unblocks full drawing parity inside animation (the user's "Animation is missing all of the capabilities Drawing should have" report).

- **#1882 — Resume "Edit" still mints a duplicate studio project for resumes saved before subject-linking** — `/studio?editResume=<id>` now find-or-creates: it reuses the document project LINKED to the resume subject and only mints (with the subject link) on first edit, and `StudioLanding` renders the loading shell instead of the chooser so the handoff goes straight to the editor (fixed this pass in `StudioLanding.tsx` + `use-create-studio-draft.ts`). But projects created BEFORE this change have no `studio_subjects` row for the resume, so the lookup misses them and a single new (correctly-linked) project is still minted the next time they're edited — thereafter deduped. Fixing it fully: a one-off backfill that links each existing `mediaKind:"document"` project to the `resume`/`article` id stored in its `documentState.entityId`. Unblocks zero-duplicate edit for legacy resumes.

- **#1883 — Resume print/PDF export diverges from the canvas layout for studio-authored resumes** — `/resumes/:id` now renders canvas-authored resumes (those with `content.meta.documentLayout`) through the shared `<DocumentPagedView>`/`<DocumentView>` paged preview canvas, and template-switching re-skins the layout via `applyDocumentTemplate` (both fixed this pass in `ResumeDetail.tsx`). But the `?print=1` path (`ResumeDetail.tsx` print-mode early return) and the Export→PDF/Word/Text/JSON flow (`downloadResume`) still go through `DeclarativeResumeRenderer` + the descriptor — so for a canvas resume the on-screen preview no longer matches the exported PDF (breaks "preview === render === print"). Fixing it: branch the print-mode return and `downloadResume` on `documentLayout` presence, rendering `<DocumentView forPrint>` (the same path `printDocument` uses in the editor) for canvas resumes. Unblocks WYSIWYG export parity.

- **#1884 — `DocumentPagedView` paginates by naive height-windowing (can slice a line/section mid-row)** — the new "Individual Pages" two-up spread (editor stage + resume viewer + `DocumentPreviewOverlay`) windows ONE continuous render into page-height slices (`top: -pageIndex*height`), matching how the browser `@page` slices the PDF but with no block-level break avoidance — a section header or a bullet can be cut across the page boundary. Fixing it: measure flow-block offsets and insert page-break spacers so blocks don't straddle a boundary (CSS `break-inside: avoid` for the print path + an equivalent measure-and-pad pass for the windowed preview). Also note the editor's "Individual Pages" mode is review-only (read-only); authoring stays in "One Page". Unblocks clean multi-page pagination.

- **#1885 — Marketplace resume-template preview could blank the whole page on malformed resume content** — `/marketplace/templates/:slug` renders resume templates via `DeclarativeResumeRenderer` against `SAMPLE_RESUME` (or the user's own resume via the in-page source selector). It renders fine for sample data (verified headless, authed + anon), but two unguarded vectors crashed it on real data: a `skillEvidence` row with a missing `skillName` (`ItemSkillBadges` did `ev.skillName.toLowerCase()`) and a null `resume.content` (`renderSectionBody` read `data.work`). Both are now guarded, and the preview pane is wrapped in a component-level `<ErrorBoundary>` so a future render fault degrades to an inline message (with the exact stack in the SuperAdmin/developer view) instead of taking down the page. Residual: the EXACT field that triggered the user's report couldn't be reproduced locally (needs their resume row); if it recurs, the inline boundary now surfaces the precise error to pin it. Unblocks crash-free template previewing against arbitrary saved resumes.

- **#1958 — 3D-world play-mode camera view (first/third person) is runtime-only, not author-persistable** — added 1st/3rd-person camera toggle to the world-3d play runtime this pass (`V` key + on-canvas button in `GameStage3D.tsx`; `cameraView` threaded through `Scene3D` → `PlayerController`, which orbits the camera behind a visible `AvatarFigure` in third-person). The choice lives in `GameStage3D` `useState`, defaulting to first-person on every play-session entry — so an author can't set their world's default view, and the player's last choice doesn't persist across reloads. Fixing it: add an optional `defaultCameraView?: "first" | "third"` to `World3DState` (seed via `emptyWorld3DState`), expose it in the Game3DPropertiesPanel / world-settings rail, and seed the runtime `cameraView` from it. Unblocks "this is a third-person platformer" authored worlds + remembered player preference.

- **#1959 — Player avatar in third-person isn't author-selectable from the character roster** — the local third-person avatar (`PlayerController` → `AvatarFigure`) and remote-peer avatars (`PeerAvatars`) both derive their body color deterministically from the player's `userId` (`colorForId` in `PlayerAvatar.tsx`). The studio's SPRITES & ASSETS rail shows a four-hero character roster (`Player (yellow/blue/green/red)` from `sprite-library.ts`), but choosing one has no effect on the 3D avatar — those sprites only place as textured `block` entities in the 3D world. Fixing it: add a per-player avatar selection (color and/or the roster character) carried on `World3DState.spawn` or a new `player` field, feed it to `PlayerController.playerColor`, and broadcast it so peers render the chosen look. Unblocks "pick your character" in 3D worlds.

- **#1960 — Third-person avatar is a static figure (no walk/idle/jump animation)** — `AvatarFigure` is a rigid block humanoid; in third-person it slides without limb motion and doesn't react to jump/fall state. The figure also only yaws to the camera heading, not to the actual movement direction (strafing looks like moonwalking). Fixing it: drive a simple procedural walk cycle (leg/arm swing keyed to horizontal speed) + a jump pose keyed to `groundedRef`, and optionally face the velocity vector when moving. Unblocks a believable third-person character instead of a gliding statue.

Findings #1961–#1971. Verdict: backend service + shared-logic tests are broadly present; the deficits are concentrated in **untested money/security paths**, **marketing-page bodies that were never updated**, and **near-total absence of new gamification badges + editorial content** for the new surfaces. (Resume-feedback test + feedback-gamification gaps already tracked as #1950 / #1952.)

- **#1972 — Test depth: DB-orchestration seams reach `getDb()`/singletons directly, not DI, so they're covered only at the pure-logic layer** — `EngagementPayoutService.runForPeriod` (ledger write + idempotency + run-summary), the cohort/assignment mutation methods (`createCohort` company path, `addMember`/`removeMember`, `fanOutEnrollments` + notifications), and `SourcingListingService.placeBid/acceptBid` (auto-reject-losers UPDATE + winner snapshot) all instantiate their db/ledger inside the method. Tests pin the formulas + gates + decision logic; the surrounding Drizzle writes are unverified. Fixing it: thread the db/ledger through the constructor (matching `peopleOpsService`'s DI seam) so a fake-db can drive the full flow. - **#1973 — Bookings award helpers can't fire: no registered earner + no `completed` transition** — `onSessionBooked` is unwireable because `BookingsService.createReservation` always stores `bookerUserId: null` (the public `POST /public/reservations` flow is auth-free; the booker is an email/name, not an account). `onSessionCompleted` has no seam at all — nothing in the codebase ever sets `bookingReservations.status = "completed"` (the documented `pending_payment → confirmed → completed` lifecycle is unimplemented; grep finds only filter/query reads of that status). Fixing it: (a) capture the booker's userId when an authed user books, and (b) implement the session-completion transition (host marks done / post-session webhook), then wire both award helpers. - **#1974 — "References" are contact listings, not peer recommendations — no giver/receiver to award** — `onReferenceGiven`/`onReferenceReceived` are unwired because `routes/references.ts` models an owner's OWN reference *contacts* (name/email they list + selectively share), not a peer-written recommendation with a registered giver and subject. `/api/users/me/recommendations` is a stub returning `[]`. Fixing it: build the peer-recommendation surface (a registered user writes/attests a reference for another user) and wire the two award helpers to it. Unblocks reference-network gamification + a real social-proof artifact.

- **#1975 — Geo-map discovery surface (`/map`) remains unbuilt** — `MapPage.tsx` was added then removed in the 2-week window; `EventDiscoveryPanel.tsx` comments note `/map` was folded into `/tasks`. The `content_locations` data + `LocationsSitemap`/`ResourceMap` components exist, but there is no interactive map page that plots jobs/events/people/resources by geo. Fixing it: build a `MapPage` over the existing geocoder cache + `content_locations`, route it, and register PAGE_SEO. Unblocks visual geo discovery across every location-tagged entity.

- **#1976 — Cohort assignment-completion award only fires on COURSE pass, not PATH completion** — `onCohortAssignmentCompleted` is wired at the course-pass seam (`routes/courses.ts` `flipToPassed`) via a new `AssignmentService.findCompletableForLearnerSubject`, but learning-PATH assignment completion (which fans out through the path-completion path, not a single course pass) does not award. Fixing it: hook the same helper into the path-completion fan-out so path-type cohort assignments also credit the learner. Unblocks complete cohort-assignment gamification parity.

- **#1977 — Pre-existing `tsc` failures surfaced during the tools-localization pass (NOT caused by it)** — `frontend/npm run typecheck` reports 8 errors, all in files untouched by the localization work: (a) `components/dashboard/DashboardFeed.tsx:87,105` — `FeedHeading`'s prop is typed `(k: string, d?: string) => string` but receives i18next's `TFunction`, which is no longer assignable (TS2322); fix is to widen the prop type to `TFunction` (or `ReturnType<typeof useTranslation>["t"]`). (b) `lib/services/feed-service.ts:230,241,255,269,316,389` — Zod `*Schema.parse(...)`/`.data` results are returned as `FeedPost`/`FeedPostsResponse` but the inferred schema shape drifted from the hand-written types (TS2322); fix is to realign `FeedPostSchema`/`FeedPostsResponseSchema` with `FeedPost`/`FeedPostsResponse` (or derive the types from the schemas via `z.infer`). These were latent behind TypeScript's incremental cache and became visible once `lib/card-feed.ts` (widely imported) was edited for tool-card localization, widening the recheck closure. Unblocks a green `typecheck`/CI.

- **#1978 — Residual non-card tool-page strings intentionally left in English during the localization pass** — every `/tools/*` card + page user-facing string is now localized via `tools.card.<id>.*` (catalog seam `lib/tools/localize-tool.ts`) and `tools.<camelName>.*` (per-page), across `en`/`es`/`fr-CA`. Two classes were deliberately NOT translated: (a) Career360 wheel `coachPrompt` strings in `pages/tools/Career360.tsx` (`OUTER_BLUEPRINT`/`INNER_BLUEPRINT`) — these are LLM instructions sent to the AI Coach, not display text, so they stay English on purpose; (b) the `recordRun` history-summary payloads in `ProfileAudit.tsx` (and similar tool-run-recorder `summary`/`strengths`/`weaknesses` strings) that interpolate English AI-generated content — the recommendation *titles* are localized but the blended summary bodies are not. Revisit if/when the AI Coach accepts a target-language hint or tool-history rendering localizes record metadata.
- **#1990 — Gig marketplace read endpoints are uncached** — the #101 gig frontend light-up added `GET /api/gigs` (public browse — read-heavy), `/api/gigs/me`, `/api/gigs/me/bids`, and `/api/gigs/me/work`, all of which hit Postgres on every request via `GigService`. Per the caching invariant a new read path must be cached or justify why not. Fixing it: route `listOpenProjects` through `getOrSetCached` with a version-token key (the open-gig keyspace is unbounded) invalidated on create/award/cancel; cache the per-user `me*` reads under a user-scoped key invalidated on the owner's create/bid/award/status-write. Unblocks browse-grid scale without N round-trips per visit.

- **#1991 — Gig marketplace surfaces are hardcoded English** — `pages/GigMarketplace.tsx`, `GigCreatePage.tsx`, `GigDetail.tsx`, `components/creator/GigsPanel.tsx`, and `components/gigs/GigBidDialog.tsx` ship literal English strings, diverging from the tools-localization SSoT pattern (`tools.*` catalog, en/es/fr-CA — see #1978). Fixing it: lift the gig strings into a `gigs.*` i18n namespace and translate across the three locales. Unblocks i18n parity for the gig product.

- **#1992 — `TaskDTO → TaskUIState` mapping is duplicated** — `components/creator/GigsPanel.tsx`'s `toUIState` replicates the inline DTO→UI mapping in `pages/Tasks.tsx` `loadTasks` (taskType/status passthrough, `ymd()` date coercion, default `priority: "medium"`). Fixing it: extract a shared `taskDtoToUIState(dto)` into `types/task.ts` and consume it in both the Tasks page and GigsPanel (DRY). Surfaced building the reusable `<TaskBoard>`; the board + detail sheet were extracted, but this one mapper was left inlined to avoid widening the Tasks.tsx refactor blast radius.

- **#1993 — Gig award records a payout accrual but does not hold escrow at award time** — `GigService.awardBid` moves the project to `in_progress` and materialises tasks, and `POST /api/gigs/milestones/:id/release` records a `payoutLedgerService.recordAccrual` (10% fee) on release, but no Stripe PaymentIntent is held when the bid is awarded — funds are only ledger-accrued on release, not escrowed up front. The true milestone-escrow hold is tracked at **#1767** (Stripe Connect escrow) and dispute resolution at **#1768**; this entry just records that the new frontend ships on top of the accrual-only flow until #1767 lands. Also: `GigDetail` shows the bidder's display name only (no avatar / profile link), and gig work items are created with a fixed `taskType: Project` + `priority: medium`.

- **#1994 — Pre-existing `tsc` errors in `api/src/db/schema/localizations.ts` (NOT caused by the gig work)** — `api/npm run typecheck` reports 5 errors in `localizations.ts` only: lines 11–13 need explicit `.js` import extensions under `nodenext` (TS2835), and lines 32/53 reference an unimported `unique` from drizzle-orm (TS2304). Untouched by the gig marketplace pass (confirmed: the 5 errors are the entire `tsc` error set and none are in gig/task files). Fixing it: add the `.js` extensions and import `unique` from `drizzle-orm/pg-core`. Unblocks a green api `typecheck`.

### Employer Pricing-page marketing-claim audit — 2026-06-13 (overclaims vs shipped reality)

Cross-checked every bullet on the employer FREE + paid-suite pricing copy against shipped schema/routes/UI. 23 of 25 claims verified real (ATS+JSON-LD, CRM, video screening, Chrome extension, seat/token limits, company follow, multi-tenant CHRO, Engage/Inform/Inspire community, segment-isolated embeds, Dropbox-Sign offers + onboarding checklists, OKRs/reviews, Brand-Kit studio promos, in-video lead forms, async interviews, SCORM/xAPI/certs, classrooms, ATS connectors + OpenAPI 3.1, white-label subdomain, affiliate tiers, Gmail/Outlook inbox sync). **Two prior "overclaim" suspicions were false alarms** and are recorded here so they aren't re-flagged: *priority-ranked "smart notifications"* IS shipped (`notifications.ts GET /smart`, Premium — see route table) and *two-way calendar sync* IS shipped (`calendar.ts`, Google+Outlook OAuth). The two genuine gaps:

- **#2008 — Pricing page advertises a "DEI funnel" employer analytics view that does not exist** — the paid-suite "Advanced analytics" bullet lists "DEI funnel" alongside time-to-hire / source mix / audit log (all of which ARE shipped: `analytics.ts /time-to-hire`+`/hiring-metrics`, `job-analytics.ts` source-mix + `pipelineFunnel`, `userAuditLog.ts`). There is no diversity dimension on any analytics surface. The data foundation is only partially registered: the consent-gated **Diversity self-ID taxonomy (#236)** and **Diversity sourcing filter (#220)** are both still Open/P2 — neither is a hiring-funnel analytics rollup, and nothing reads them into a DEI funnel chart. Fixing it: either drop "DEI funnel" from the marketing copy until built, or ship a consent-gated diversity-funnel rollup on top of #236 (EEOC-isolated, reads only consented rows). Unblocks an honest analytics claim + the diversity-reporting story.

- **#2009 — Inbox-Sync add-on pricing ("3 mailboxes per user, +$5/mo each") is unwired and contradicts the README** — pricing copy advertises 3 mailboxes per user with a "+$5/mo each" paid add-on. The 3-mailbox cap + Pro gate are real and enforced (`email-integration.ts`, "3-inbox cap" comment), but (a) no `$5`/per-mailbox add-on price exists anywhere in `shared/pricing.ts` or the billing config — the `inboxSeatAddonService` reference has no wired amount, and (b) the README route/feature notes describe the 3 mailboxes as **"included"** (#875/#1313), not as a paid add-on. So the marketing introduces a metered add-on that is neither priced in code nor consistent with the internal spec. Fixing it: decide included-vs-metered, then either wire the $5 add-on SKU into `pricing.ts` + entitlement-catalog and reconcile #875/#1313, or correct the copy to "3 mailboxes included." Unblocks accurate inbox-sync billing.

*(Data-residency note: the copy presents "data-residency policy" affirmatively while storage is single-region US/Neon — but this is already recorded as roadmap at the Launch-Blocker line "SOC 2 / SSO / data residency are listed as roadmap, not on Pricing.tsx" and the multi-region PRD; no new entry opened.)*

Fixing it: mint a per-connection webhook URL with an embedded opaque token (`/webhook/:provider/:token`) and look the connection up by token. Unblocks correct multi-company webhook routing.

- **#2017 — ATS webhook stage changes don't reach `job_applications`** — #2014 mirrors webhook candidates into `talent_pool_candidates` + `candidate_interactions`, but a stage-change event is not reflected on the internal `job_applications` pipeline because there is no external-job-id ↔ `job_items.id` mapping. Fixing it: add an `ats_job_map` table (provider + external job id → internal job) populated at connect/sync time, then upsert applications + stage on stage-change webhooks. Unblocks true ATS↔pipeline stage mirroring.

- **Audit note (2026-06-21) — "senior-executives confidential-search has no exec-specific mode" was a FALSE POSITIVE, no gap filed** — the capability already ships: [ConfidentialModeToggle](frontend/components/settings/ConfidentialModeToggle.tsx) is mounted in Settings → **Privacy** ([Settings.tsx](frontend/pages/Settings.tsx), migrations [0169_confidential_search_mode](api/drizzle/0169_confidential_search_mode.sql) + [0174_confidential_blocklist](api/drizzle/0174_confidential_blocklist.sql)). It hides the profile from the public people directory AND blocks specific employers (e.g. current employer) while staying visible to other recruiters — exactly what the [confidential_search focus feature](shared/audiences-registry.ts) promises, and `/settings?tab=privacy` resolves to the tab it lives in. (Recorded as a note, not a numbered row — the audit's interim id collided with the existing #2240 contact-email gap and was dropped.)

## Implementation Status & Coverage Inventories (moved from README 2026-06-20)

Shipped-capability matrices and implementation-status inventories relocated out of the README so it stays focused on architecture + open work. Open items referenced below remain tracked in the [Consolidated Gap Register](ROADMAP.md#consolidated-gap-register).
### Video Studio Capability Assessment


Evaluated against a feature specification for a fully browser-based general-purpose video editor comparable to Canva Video / CapCut. hired.video's studio is purpose-built for AI-driven video resume and employer content creation, not a traditional non-linear editor (NLE). The table below documents parity, partial coverage, and open gaps against that specification.

**Summary: 31 ✅ fully implemented · 4 ⚠️ partial · 3 ❌ not implemented (38 capabilities total)**

Open gaps against the Canva-Video / CapCut spec are tracked in the [Consolidated Gap Register](#consolidated-gap-register) as entries #124–#133. Net-new studio gaps beyond that spec (AI avatars, dubbing, audio enhancement, multi-platform publishing, in-video lead capture, chapters, thumbnails, hook optimizer, etc.) are tracked as #134–#145.

#### Core Requirements

| Capability | Status | Implementation | Gap Register |
|---|---|---|---|
| Timeline-based editor | ✅ Done | `NLETimeline.tsx` — frame ruler with click-to-seek, draggable scene blocks, playhead, zoom (20–240 px/s). Mounted below the preview canvas in `StudioLayout.tsx`. | — |
| Video, audio, image, and text tracks | ✅ Done | Scene blocks decompose into the existing canvas node graph (text/image/video). Multi-track audio mixer (#129) covers music + voiceover lanes. | — |
| Clip trimming, splitting, merging, reordering | ✅ Done | `scene-ops.ts` — `trimScene`, `splitSceneAtTime`, `mergeWithNext` (seamless re-merge of contiguous trim points), `reorderScene`. Surfaced as drag handles + S/M/D/Del shortcuts in `NLETimeline.tsx`. | — |
| Multi-layer editing with precision timing | ⚠️ Partial | `animation-graph.ts` supports per-node keyframe interpolation under the hood; visual keyframe editor not yet exposed. | — |

| Voice Marketplace | ✅ Done | Creators upload a reference sample (`POST /api/studio/voice-clones`, private by default), set their own price, and toggle `Monetize` to publish (`PATCH /:id` with consent). Listings appear in the homepage `Voices` category and `VoiceMarketplaceCard` adds them to the shopping cart. Buyers receive a perpetual personal license (`studio_voice_clone_licenses`) with 95/5 creator/platform split + CC processing fee charged to the buyer (per #156). All synthesis runs in the buyer's browser via VibeVoice — the server never runs a model. Schema: `studio_voice_clones` (extended with `visibility`, `price_cents`, `platform_fee_bps`, `consent_*`), `studio_voice_clone_licenses`. Routes: `GET /voice-clones/library`, `GET /voice-clones/marketplace`, `PATCH /voice-clones/:id`, `POST /voice-clones/:id/claim`, `POST /voice-clones/cart-checkout`. Terms of Service §9a covers consent, ownership, and the revenue split. | — |

### Legacy API Coverage Map


This section documents every controller in `/myvideoresume-api` (31 C# controllers, ~200 endpoints), the business-logic service it calls, the DB tables it touches, and whether the TypeScript API has a matching implementation.

**Coverage key:**
✅ Fully covered — TypeScript API has equivalent endpoints with DB-backed logic
⚠️ Partial — Routes exist but logic is stubbed, missing, or incomplete
❌ Not covered — No equivalent in TypeScript API

#### Can the legacy project be removed?

**Short answer: Not yet — Stripe is the blocker.**

The TypeScript API covers ~89% of the legacy surface area. All remaining legacy-parity gaps are tracked in the [Consolidated Gap Register](#consolidated-gap-register) (`legacy-parity` type). The Stripe blocker items below have since been resolved.

| Missing | Risk | Status |
|---------|------|--------|
| `POST /payment/stripe/webhook` | **🔴 High** | ✅ Implemented |
| `GET /payment/public-key` | **🔴 High** | ✅ Implemented |
| `POST /payment/setup-intent` | **🔴 High** | ✅ Implemented |
| `POST /payment/save-payment-method` | **🔴 High** | ✅ Implemented |
| `GET /api/export/csv` + `GET /api/export/excel` | 🟡 Medium | Open — see Gap Register #31 |
| Recruiter bulk ops (`bulk/tags`, `bulk/status`, `bulk/delete`) | 🟡 Medium | Open — see Gap Register #32 |
| `GET /api/recruiter/talent-pool/export` | 🟢 Low | Open — see Gap Register #33 |
| `POST /api/passwordmanagement/validate-history` | 🟢 Low | Open — see Gap Register #34 |
| `GET /api/passwordmanagement/is-expired` | 🟢 Low | Open — see Gap Register #35 |
| `GET /api/resume/:id/diff` | 🟢 Low | Open — see Gap Register #36 |
| Chrome extension endpoints (`ChromeController`) | ✅ None — marked `[Obsolete]` in legacy | Fully replaced by `/api/match/*` |
| OData endpoints (ApplicationUsers/Roles) | ✅ None | Not needed for edge runtime |

**Checklist to safely delete `/myvideoresume-api`:**

- [x] ✅ `GET /api/payment/public-key` — returns `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` env var
- [x] ✅ `POST /api/payment/setup-intent` — creates Stripe SetupIntent, returns `clientSecret`
- [x] ✅ `POST /api/payment/save-payment-method` — attaches PM to customer, upserts to DB, sets default
- [x] ✅ `POST /api/payment/stripe/webhook` — signature verified; handles `subscription.created/updated/deleted`, `invoice.payment_succeeded/failed`, `payment_method.attached/detached`, `payout.paid/failed`; records affiliate conversions
- [ ] (Optional) Add CSV serialisation to `/api/settings/export`

**The legacy project can now be safely deleted once Stripe secrets are configured.**

Configure secrets:
```bash
wrangler secret put STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY    # pk_live_...
wrangler secret put STRIPE_SECRET_KEY         # sk_live_...
wrangler secret put STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY # whsec_...
```

Register webhook in Stripe dashboard → Developers → Webhooks:
- **URL:** `https://api.hired.video/api/payment/stripe/webhook`
- **Events:** `customer.subscription.*`, `invoice.payment_succeeded`, `invoice.payment_failed`, `payment_method.attached`, `payment_method.detached`, `payout.paid`, `payout.failed`
